staring blankly at the crowd in the subway station.
The call was from the parent of a ninth-grade boy I tutor. A grandparent was in the hospital,
and the whole family was going to visit, so this morning's session was canceled.
Add to that the high schooler I was supposed to teach this afternoon coming down with a fever,
which meant that today... had suddenly opened up.
With zero warning, a whole day off had been shoved into my hands.
Since when... had I become unable to adjust to a “day off”?
I used to be a guy who was lying flat—even taking jobs, I was totally Zen about it.
But ever since Xiaoqi came along, my days had somehow turned into a grind... a voluntary one.
She's always springing little surprises on me, and our personalities just click.
Life with her feels full... and even when it's busy, I don't feel tired.
How did I spend my days back when I was lying flat?
I wasn't giving up, even then. Even my rest time ran on a fixed plan.
Exercise, basketball, strolls through the library or a museum...
Even going to the internet café—it was all scheduled in advance.
So having a free day dumped on me out of nowhere left me a bit at a loss.
...Head home first, maybe? Or stop by the market for groceries?
With Xiaoqi out, I could clean the place and air out the comforter,
and if all else fails, do some research at home to prep for future work.
I shut the door on pure instinct,
and just as I was about to apologize, I realized something was off.
Wait, that's my girlfriend. What am I panicking for...
「Hahaha, Hu Lai's instinctive reaction is too adorable!」
「Why hide when your girlfriend's changing? You've looked plenty of times before.」
「Basic courtesy still exists, you know... And you really caught me off guard.」
「Why are you back? What were you doing just now?」
「Taking a shower! A street-sprinkler truck got me on the way home and soaked me.」
「Hold on... shouldn't you be at work today? Why are you home at this hour?」
「One of the aunties at our place was on weekend duty, but her son's birthday is this weekend, so she wanted to swap with me.」
「I figured you'd be out teaching this weekend anyway, and I'd be bored home alone, so I said sure.」
「Huh? Why are you home at this hour too?」
「Both my students canceled today, so I came back to rest.」
「Swapping shifts was the right call! Time for just the two of us! Couple time~」
「By the way, haven't you gone out with your old friends lately? Rare free time—you could make some plans.」
「It's a workday. Hardly anyone can get away.」
「Besides, yours truly has a boyfriend now, and everyone knows better than to intrude.」
「...What does that have to do with anything.」
「Everything! I went public on Moments ages ago, okay! With all my daily lovey-dovey posts, nobody wants to be the third wheel.」
「What's there to fear? 'Flaunting love ends in death'? I work at a funeral home—I fear everything except death.」
「What I mean is... hang out with your friends more, like before. It'd spice up your Moments feed too.」
「Whoa, Mr. Hu is that open-minded? You don't want to monopolize your girlfriend's time?」
「A normal social life is still necessary.」
「That dinner-meetup group chat you joined—still active?」
「Yep, they organize stuff all the time.」
「How come I haven't seen you go lately?」
「Can't help it. Hubby's cooking is too good—I can't stomach the pre-made stuff outside anymore.」
「Yes, yes, all your fault for spoiling my appetite!」
「I'm just suggesting you see your friends regularly, like before.」
「Something's off. Why does it feel... like you keep trying to push me out the door?」
「We suddenly have a free day—don't you want to spend it with me?」
「Ah! I've got it! Today's Hu Lai is a little—flus—tered!」
「Think about it. On our dates, or lazy days at home, you always had everything mapped out.」
「Where to go, which route, where to eat, what to do at home, what snacks to have... You planned it all so thoroughly.」
「But today the plan got suddenly wrecked—aren't you a little rattled?」
「Not rattled, exactly... I just like to have some preparation before doing things.」
「Hahaha, just like prepping lesson plans—an occupational hazard.」
「Having a plan just puts my mind at ease.」
「Haha, I know it's you looking out for me, and that makes me really happy.」
「But when we're together, being loose and casual is nice too. Having no plan is also a plan.」
「...Zero preparation might make me a little anxious.」
「Great, great! Today I get to watch my boyfriend have an anxious day!」
「Life needs a little seasoning~ Gotta see my boyfriend flustered once in a while.」
「So what were you planning to do when you got back?」
「Chores? We haven't really tidied up these past few days.」
「Then let's do them together! Give me half the chores, otherwise I look totally useless.」
「Sure, let's start. Help me air out the sheets.」
「Whooah—! Stretching the old muscles feels great! Many hands really do make light work!」
「Yeah, chores go faster with two people.」
「Exactly~ So from now on, we can do everything together! Double the efficiency!」
「Even showers—we could scrub each other's backs. Wouldn't that save half the time?」
「Haha, when we're seventy or eighty and our arms won't reach around anymore, we'll have no choice but to wipe each other down—what a heartwarming image.」
Seventy or eighty... I can't even imagine it...
By then she'll definitely be one of those little old ladies who runs the scene.
...At the very least she'd lead a square-dancing troupe—the kind that rules the whole park.
「Recharging! Hugging hubby to get my HP back.」
「So what's the plan next? Think about it.」
「...No plan. We finished the chores too fast.」
「Some CS? If not, we team up and stomp randoms.」
「We played for three hours yesterday. My head still hurts.」
「Then... want some quality time with your adorable wifey?」
「Then binge a show with me? There's an anime I didn't finish from a few days ago.」
「Sure... I don't feel like prepping lessons right now anyway.」
「Yay! Finally watching something together! Let me grab some snacks—」
「Such a sweet girl... how could she just die like that...」
「She was cursed. Nothing to be done.」
「That's why I asked why you'd pick a tearjerker. Here, tissues.」
「—How did you bounce back that fast!?」
「Well, you cry when it's time to cry, and eat when it's time to eat.」
「The heroine's tragic, but I've got a great boyfriend. I'm happy.」
「Making lunch is probably too late—want to just grab something downstairs?」
「Sure! Then let's hit that Lanzhou noodle place—they pile on way more meat than anyone else!」
「If you're too lazy to change, I'll go get takeout.」
「...And I can pick up yesterday's packages while I'm at it. There are a lot of them.」
「Oh? Hu Lai, actually having a pile of packages? That's new.」
「Whoa! Did you go stock up at a wholesale market today?」
「It's that thing you used to play with all the time... unclaimed-parcel mystery boxes.」
「I had a moment of weakness and bought one to try.」
「Hahahaha, you fell into that pit too!」
「Very nice, very nice. They say married couples grow to resemble each other—seems it's true.」
「Oh, right, there was a note when I bought it—said it was a men-only mystery box.」
「Probably guessed from the recipient's name, I'd imagine...」
「Who cares! Open it, open it, open it—」
「Cheap junk. I'll keep them for scrubbing shoes.」
「Exactly, exactly—now we have a couples set of toothbrushes~」
「This quality... they'd fall apart after two wears.」
「Keep them? We'll bring them when we travel—wear twice, then toss.」
「Ahahaha, a hair clip! Wasn't this a men-only box?」
「Maybe it's meant as a gift for the girlfriend.」
「Give her this, and she'd run off in a huff, wouldn't she?」
「Then how about I give it to you?」
「If it's from you, I'll keep it. Whatever junk you give me, I want it.」
「You say that like everything I've given you before was junk...」
「Don't! No-name products off my face, please! What if I break out!」
「Huh? Fine then. My boyfriend's face is precious. Can't take risks!」
「What kind of trashy read? Let me see—How... to... Win... Over... Beautiful Girls.」
「You have to study this seriously! Learn it well! Conquer me soon, hahaha—」
「Sure. I've been wondering how to handle you—now I can pick up some tips.」
I can't believe books like this exist...
That's actually impressive... This thing's practically an artifact.
「Hm? What's this? A whole big bag.」
The newly opened box was full of little paper sheets.
「The sticky kind. You put them on your skin and pretend you have a tattoo.」
「Hahaha, even tattoos can be fake—so you can fake being edgy, huh!」
「Yeah... not everyone dares to ink designs on their own skin.」
Some girls fake being rebellious by covering themselves in designs.
Then they regret it quickly—except real tattoos don't come off that easily.
「What now? What did you open this time?」
「What the hell did you stick on? Wipe it off!」
「Trendy my ass—if you're going to stick something on, at least pick a normal design!」
「Hahaha, he's embarrassed! Hu Lai's actually embarrassed!」
「You're totally into this, aren't you? You like bad-girl rebels, don't you?!」
「This isn't rebellion, it's brain damage! Wipe it off right now!」
「There's a whole box left! I'll put some on you too!」
「Hahaha, there's even a 'Loyal to the Nation' one here! I'll stick it on your back!」
For the next stretch of time, we covered each other's faces with all sorts of ridiculous things.
It was great fun—but then we spent another half hour washing it all off.
Granted, the wish of showering together and wiping each other down did come true...
But most of it went to scrubbing off these damned tattoo stickers.
These things are seriously hard to scrub off...
「I'm happy! I had so much fun playing with hubby.」
「You were covered in red and purple blotches—I had to scrub forever to get it all off you.」
「It's fine, it's fine. This girl's got thick skin.」
「Haha, fine, fine. The more hubby laughs at me, the happier I am.」
「What? I need to go wash the dishes.」
「Was dinner okay? Was the sour-cabbage fish maybe a little bland?」
「It was amazing! When has anything hubby made ever not been delicious!」
「A lot of things. Especially for working so hard at being a good husband.」
「Isn't that just what I should do?」
「It's exactly because you think it's what you should do that I'm thanking you.」
「But you don't have to be this serious all the time from now on. Loosen up—going with the flow is even better.」
「I like you when you're serious. And I like you when you're not, too.」
「So don't put so much pressure on yourself. Whatever feels comfortable, go with that.」
「You said it. From now on, I'll just wing it.」
「That's right, that's right—Hu Lai should be reckless!」
「...What's wrong... spacing out all of a sudden.」
「It just feels... like maybe you're so... well-trained because you had a girlfriend before?」
「I've been single since birth. Where would an ex-girlfriend come from?」
「We were never like that. We did used to be fairly close, though.」
「Besides, she's an extremely demanding person—about her career, her life, and the people around her.」
「Of course, she holds others to high standards, but herself to even higher ones... that's how she built the company.」
「Working alongside her, drilled by her high standards for years—that's where some of my habits came from.」
In that sense, maybe I should be thanking her.
The pity is, that woman only loved the feeling of winning,
and never cared why she was doing it in the first place.
「No rush! You promised me half the chores. Right now... I just want to hold you a little longer.」
「So how did today feel—a totally unprepared, off-plan day?」
「It felt strange at first. Now I think it was really nice.」
「Good! Let's keep it like this from now on. No pressure.」
「Live a plain, happy life, then walk hand in hand into the coffin—that's the best ending there is!」
「Don't drop a line straight out of the underworld like that...」
「Hahahaha, force of habit, force of habit.」
「Use extra dish soap. The sour-cabbage fish was pretty oily.」
「So, um... a girlfriend who works hard on chores deserves a big reward tonight.」
「And just so you know, this time I have zero preparation. Whatever happens, happens.」
「—Bring it on! I'm not scared of you! I'll be waiting!」
And so the go-with-the-flow day ended, well, by going with the flow.
I'd been a lie-flat guy for years, but I'd never truly lain flat.
The good news is, now that I have her, whether I lie flat or not... I'll be accepted. I'll be loved.
It looks like Hu Lai and Xiaoqi's “reckless” life together is going to last a lifetime.
「Welcome to the show. Our guest today is a phenomenon in the education industry these past few years—」
「The company she founded, LaiJuan Education, specializes in premium gaokao college-consulting services—and even at steep prices, the clients keep coming.」
「Please give a warm round of applause to the CEO of LaiJuan Education, Lin Juan—Boss Lin!」
「Boss Lin, why don't you start by saying a few words to everyone?」
「A lot of people are taken aback the first time they hear the name 'LaiJuan Education.' Is that deliberately playing on people's anxiety?」
「It simply blends the names of the company's two founders. Besides, in today's climate, no one needs us to manufacture anxiety.」
「People actually have a lot of questions about you and LaiJuan Education. About the fees, for instance—」
「They say your top-tier gaokao consulting package costs nearly as much as an ordinary family makes in a year.」
「Many ask: is a list of college preferences really worth that much money?」
「First, I won't dodge the question of high fees. LaiJuan Education does charge well above the industry average.」
「But I'll say this: our value far exceeds that price.」
「Gaokao preferences aren't just 'picking a few schools.' It's choosing the track your child will run for the next ten, twenty years of their life—」
「The right major saves five or ten years of detours; the right school and city bring more resources and opportunities.」
「That money isn't paying for 'filling out a form.' It's paying to 'help your child win at the starting line.' Kids from ordinary families don't get many chances to make mistakes.」
「One right choice can cancel out years of being behind. That's the confidence behind our prices—and why so many parents are willing to pay.」
「True, the importance of choice goes without saying. But shouldn't that choice be based on the child's interests?」
「I never deny the value of interests. But I must remind everyone plainly: you can't eat interests for breakfast.」
「Especially for kids from ordinary families, choosing by interest is often the most extravagant—and the riskiest—option.」
「I'm not the cynical one. The world is.」
「At least for now—this world is still winner-take-all. So hard work matters, but choosing right matters even more.」
「Pick the right path, and your effort pays double. That's how you win in the end.」
It's true—human beings fundamentally love to "win."
From childhood we're taught to "win at the starting line,"
and as adults we fall into comparison and competition at work and in social life.
Because humans are social animals, and social animals all need to "win."
Winning doesn't just prove you're good—it's a power relation.
I'm better, so I outrank you,
my opinions are right, and you'd better listen to me.
Maybe pursuing victory isn't the problem in itself.
But once society passes its phase of rapid growth,
People put in more and more, but the returns don't grow proportionally.
When "winning" becomes the only goal worth pursuing,
"losing" becomes a humiliation too heavy to bear.
there are also people who never cared about this win-lose system to begin with.
like a drunk cat careening down the corridor.
The bathroom door slides open, then shut, followed by the rush of running water.
The water isn't hot yet at this hour, but she probably doesn't care.
The water stopped. A while later, the door on this side opened,
and the sound of wet bare feet on the floor came closer and closer.
「You'll catch a cold, and the pillow will get moldy.」
「My soul's about to leave my body...」
「Good enough. Get dressed and go to sleep.」
I turned away and waited while she barely wriggled into her clothes,
then heard her head thump onto the pillow.
Say she doesn't care about winning or losing, yet she loves playing matches against people...
Curious about everything, and completely without wariness.
What kind of environment did she grow up in?
Then again, she's a fresh graduate (or maybe not even that?),
and even after working a while, she may not know how treacherous the world is.
But it's also possible that, for certain reasons...
she's long since had some of those rules down cold.
So casual and cheeky with me—
is it because she's pegged me as a harmless target?
is she like this with everyone?
A young, pretty, sexy, open-minded girl, totally unguarded, and warm toward you...
Most men would get some ideas, then do her a few favors.
That really is how some women survive.
It's just that it tends to invite trouble...
But she doesn't seem to mind much,
because she's a troublemaker by nature.
Whatever. Care less about her business.
This is a capsule hotel—no different from a train sleeper car.
Upper bunk, lower bunk. However well you hit it off, when the stop comes, everyone goes their own way.
The current distance between her and me is just fine.
We do each other small favors, and neither expects too much.
it wouldn't be hard for her to find another crowd of guy friends.
Whoever she ends up with is her own business.
After resting a while, that familiar feeling came from beside me.
The gaze that once annoyed me...
「Oh right, Hu Lai, how tall are you?」
「Whoa... I never noticed before. How does a frame like yours even fit into a capsule?」
「You squeeze, you manage. Still roomier than the top bunk on an old green train.」
She came back this morning looking half-dead—
and she's back in shape after only four hours of sleep?
「Hey, I've always had fast HP regen! Night-shift workers have to treasure their daylight hours!」
「Besides, it's rare that classmate Hu Lai didn't run away, so of course I got up a little early to squeeze in some quality time and deepen our bond!」
「Aren't you always gone by this hour?」
「I have an interview this afternoon. Wanted more rest this morning.」
「An interview?! Is the lie-flat guy making a comeback? What job? Where?」
「Tutoring needs an interview? Isn't it show me the money and start teaching?」
「Hardly... Parents pick tutors, and tutors pick students and parents too.」
「Right. Some students don't want to learn at all, and some parents won't let you actually teach.」
「Plenty... A kid with problems is solvable. A parent with problems and I'm out of options.」
「I once tutored a ninth-grade girl. Smart kid, but her mom was extremely controlling.」
「She had to sit right next to us during lessons. Every two or three sentences from me, she'd butt in, until it became her daughter and me getting scolded together.」
「A while back I taught a high school boy who wanted humanities, but his dad forced him into science, then yelled at him for not being able to keep up.」
「I suggested his dad let him try switching to humanities... His dad pulled up some influencer's video to show me, saying humanities majors all starve.」
「Ooof... that money isn't easy to earn.」
「It's all right. At least I control my own pace.」
「When I'm busy, eight or nine thousand a month. But the mental strain is heavy... you're responsible for students, after all.」
「Normally, with fewer students and a lighter schedule... three or four thousand, give or take.」
「And when I get tired, I rest for a stretch and do other odd jobs. I was never one to spend money anyway... enough to cover my social insurance and I'm set.」
「By the way, always buy your social insurance—health insurance especially.」
「I knew a cleaning lady who had an appendectomy—the bill was terrifying! Good thing she had insurance; almost all of it was covered!」
But you haven't graduated yet, right? Isn't it a bit early to worry about that.
「So what do you do in your free time normally? What are your hobbies?」
「Hahaha, it's called chatting! You're actually here, and you're actually willing to talk to me. Rare!」
「Hobbies... honestly, I don't think I have any.」
「What about basketball? CS? Don't those count?」
「Basketball is exercise, not a hobby. CS was something I played with college roommates; now it's just how I kill time.」
「Killing time at that level? You're totally humble-bragging...」
「I'm not addicted to games. But if I'm playing, I'll figure out how to play well.」
「I see... no wonder you seem so unflappable.」
「Maybe in ten years you'll turn into a bald fishing dude...」
「Haven't tried fishing... and fishing doesn't necessarily cause baldness. Don't stereotype.」
「Hahaha, really? I feel like they're all pretty bald.」
People usually only have time to fish after they retire, okay.
「Wow! Classmate Hu Lai is finally asking about me!」
「Mm-hm! I have tons of hobbies. Recently I'm into... baking, yoga, and travel.」
「Uh... isn't that the blind-date blacklist trifecta?」
「Huh? Why would a blind date blacklist them?」
「Lots of guys, when they hear a woman's hobbies are yoga, baking, and travel, instantly blacklist her in their heads.」
「Because those three burn money and are perfect for photo ops.」
「Some people barely do them at all—their energy goes into staging photos, editing them, posting them to pump up their market value.」
「I lost out, I lost out! I've been at it this long without a single decent photo. Total loss!」
「Not a single one? Doesn't sound like you.」
「When I'm having fun, who has time for photos... Yoga's genuinely fun! I started junior year.」
「Other sports were too tiring, and I couldn't keep bouncing in cheerleading, so when the school clubs recruited, I gave it a try.」
「The yoga teacher was super nice, and I found twisting my body around fascinating—even playing dead, I could strike more advanced poses!」
「As for baking... also junior year, I think. I had this amazing cream puff at a café and pestered the pastry chef until he taught me a few tricks.」
「Oh, right! That chef's girlfriend was adorable! Even younger than me.」
「They'd hide on the café's second floor... getting cozy, pretty loud about it too! It made me want to peek!」
「Were you there to learn baking or what...」
「I did learn baking! I borrowed their equipment and made tons—fattened my whole dorm up a size!」
Everyone else got fat and you didn't—didn't that make them resent you?
「As for travel... that's totally spontaneous, basically all budget trips.」
「Freshman summer I was bored out of my mind, slung on a backpack, hopped an old green train, bought tickets at random—wherever it stopped, that was the destination.」
「I know that one... did the same thing the year I quit my job.」
「But that time I slept through my stop and got off in the middle of nowhere... wandered into this really poor village.」
「The poverty-relief cadre there was this amazing woman, so I just stuck to her like glue as her helper. Stayed over half a month!」
「There was even a flood partway through. Pretty dangerous...」
「Oh! The village had this big goose—so arrogant! One time I couldn't take it anymore and I fought it!」
「It bit me up something awful! But I didn't lose either—I twisted the feathers right off its butt!」
「Ah well... when I got back after summer I was so tan my own mom wouldn't recognize me. For months I had to go full tanned-gyaru style...」
She's turned the blind-date blacklist trifecta into a whole art form.
Coming from anyone else, they'd be carefully packaged labels;
from her, they're life experiences covered in mud and dusted with flour.
Other people take photos to prove "this is the life I have";
she's immersed in it purely because "living like this is fun."
「Ahh... but too bad, I'm about to graduate. Can't afford a yoga studio, no baking equipment, and no travel once I start work.」
「Welcome to working life. No one stays that free.」
「But! I've developed a new hobby recently!」
「No, no, not expensive at all—I do group feasts.」
「Yeah, I know this friend who loves to eat—round and adorable, so funny!」
「She hunts down restaurant coupons and set menus, then rounds people up in a group chat.」
「Five or six people per group, everyone splits the bill—super cheap per person! And the group's different every time, like opening a mystery box. You meet new friends constantly!」
It really suits her... Me, not a chance.
「I forgot! I made plans with them today! We agreed to meet at the mall this afternoon—no wonder I had to get up early!」
「And here I thought you got up early for me.」
「You're number one, feasts are number two!」
「That friend says I should... change my outfit? What does that mean?」
「Oh, that's normal. Your usual getup is a bit much... you'd stand out sharing a table with strangers.」
「Come to think of it... have you even changed clothes these past weeks?」
「As if! I bought five or six of the same outfit, okay! I just can't be bothered to coordinate.」
「—Wanna smell my clothes and check for odor?」
「Ah, I get it. You're the type who finds one comfortable outfit and wears it to death, finds one thing you like and eats it until you're sick of it?」
「Ooh! Hu Lai! Not bad! You're figuring me out more and more!」
She's probably the same with people...
That's why she's been clinging to me lately—she'll drop me once she's bored.
「Whatever, changing clothes is no big deal. Let me see what's at the bottom of my suitcase.」
The door opened, and the girl who'd been so rowdy a moment ago bounced in.
Navy beret, white blouse with a light blue tie,
topped with a soft, fluffy beige cardigan.
Pleated short skirt... and even a small white crossbody box bag.
She looked like she'd stepped out of some school-life manga—
the gentle, wholesome honor student type, at that.
Amazing. The switch from gyaru to this doesn't clash at all.
The outfit pressed down a bit of that rowdy energy,
turning it into something... cleaner, brighter, more youthful.
It just hit me that this girl hasn't fully entered the working world yet...
which makes this look far more natural on her.
「Hey, hey, quit staring. What's the verdict?」
With that, she deliberately hopped back a step.
「Hahaha, good reaction. This outfit change was worth it!」
「Hey! As if I'm normally so disreputable!」
「About that time. Shall we head out together?」
「I still need a while here. You go ahead.」
「No worries, I'll wait! Not in a hurry.」
「There's really no need to leave together.」
「But I want to! We've basically been living together half a month and you're still shy?」
「Besides, walking together makes it feel like a date. I put on this whole outfit—I should get something out of it, right?」
「Ah, I just noticed! You're blushing! The tips of your ears are red!」
「Does this look really do it for you? Classmate Hu Lai likes the wholesome schoolgirl style, hmm.」
「Very good, very good. Now I know just what prescription to write... For you, I can pretend. Hehe!」
「No need. The way you usually are is fine... Just being natural is the least stressful.」
「Hello? Oh, oh! You're there? Coming right now!」
「I'm off! My friends are waiting at the mall entrance up ahead!」
「Huh? You're here too!? Why not just come along? Find us after your interview!?」
「Why not? Split six ways it's really cheap!」
「How many people this time? What's the gender ratio?」
「Three guys, three girls—with me that makes six.」
「That's a default-matched setup... If I show up, the balance breaks.」
「Where are you guys? Ohh, okay, just around the corner!」
「Good luck at the interview then, classmate Hu Lai! I'm off! Bye-bye!」
These so-called group dinners, with men and women both,
come with an implicit matchmaking function.
Does she genuinely not know, or has she never cared?
Well, best wishes that she meets someone she likes. I've got things to do.
Hope the student and parents this time are reasonable...
Coming out of the café, the afternoon sun was a bit blinding.
No real loss—this time I chose to walk away myself.
I just felt a bit sorry for the kid. A tenth-grade girl, bright-eyed—
quick to answer my questions, and clear-headed too.
But her parents kept butting heads, even in front of a stranger, without holding back.
One would make a point; the other would reflexively counter it.
Her dad said, "I think she needs to shore up the fundamentals,"
and her mom immediately shot back, "What good are fundamentals? She needs to tackle hard problems to pull ahead."
The moment I said, "Her comprehension is quite good,"
the dad nodded and the mom frowned and countered, "Not at all. She can't absorb anything."
It wasn't discussion—it was reflexive opposition...
Whatever I said, if one side agreed, the other had to object.

they've sacrificed more, they know better, they love the child more.

His gaze drifted, sticking to Xiaoqi most of the time,
as if I didn't exist at all in his eyes.
I remembered now... I'd seen him at this internet café before.
Cursing and swearing while gaming at night. Not exactly a bad person,
but everything about him, from looks to vibe, screamed "best keep your distance."

This guy across from us... he's genuinely got skills.

The moment Xiaoqi reached an off-angle position, her footsteps nearly silent,
he'd turn his gun there in advance, as if he could see the future.

This time, Xiaoqi peeked out the tiniest sliver at the edge of the smoke,
and before she'd even fired, his sniper rifle was already pre-aimed and waiting there.

she deliberately took an unconventional, offbeat route, planning an ambush.

then swung out wide to finish her off... cleanly took out her side.
That game sense... almost absurdly strong.

I don't much care about being disrespected by someone like him,

I wandered over behind this guy and quietly watched his screen.

「Someone like classmate Hu Lai, nearly getting beaten up over a girl. How interesting.」

I was the one who brought her here, after all. I couldn't just stand by and let her get pushed around.
「Oh right! How did you know he was cheating?」

「Not an expert. Don't write me extra scenes.」
「When you played against me, you were going easy on me—and doing it very naturally, too. Only a fellow expert could tell.」

What was he doing here? Going online?

「Nothing... A former student. I tutored him as a side job.」
「Not anymore. But why would he come to an internet café?」

「Ohh, a good man with a sense of responsibility. That's not lying flat at all.」
「I just got to know you a little better, that's all. I'm very satisfied.」
「Hmm... hard to say... it's just a feeling.」
「Have you ever played one of those games that looks totally unremarkable, but is kind of fun once you try it?」

「The ice cream—are we still getting it or not?」
「Yes! Of course! Buy one get one free!」

If this place were fully occupied,
what kind of role would she play?
The mood-livenener, the social glue? A mediator? Or the designated troublemaker?
I'd never met a girl like this before...
Maybe it's the profession—the colleagues, clients, parents, and students I meet are all anxious.
That anxiety comes from fear, from desire, maybe from a hunger for victory.
Then again... someone like her would never go to a cram school or hire a tutor, I suppose.
「Stop reading, play a game with me!」

「I don't know what she was really thinking, or what went on in that family.」

I should feel relaxed, relieved, and drift quickly into sleep, replenishing the energy spent by accident.

to hear the faint creak of the mattress beneath me.
Somehow... I'm starting to get unused to this "pure" silence.

What was I doing just now...
Quick, I pulled that curtain shut again, sealing myself off from the outside world once more.

a small pang of regret, as if I'd missed some chance...

and with the corners of my mouth curving slightly, I slowly drifted into dreams.

sunlight streaming in right on schedule, falling on the sleeping face of the person beside me.

A completely unskilled, rather reckless kind of kiss.
Tinged with salty tears and the ragged breath that hadn't settled after her run, and she even bumped my teeth at first.
What came through even more clearly was the weight of her whole body pressed against mine,
the faint scent of her, and the smell of my old T-shirt.
That scent wasn't unfamiliar, but this was the first time it was so clear, so rich—
All those earlier musings about "lying flat" and "distance"
were washed clean away before that overbearing, unreasonable kiss.
A long-forgotten longing, one I hadn't even noticed in myself, quietly rose up inside me.
It might have been something I'd chased a very long time ago:
to be needed and trusted by someone... and then accepted, all of me.
Without having to specially "accommodate" anyone, or strain to seem "excellent."
When we finally drew apart, I noticed tiny teardrops still clinging to her lashes.
Her face was still bright red—disheveled and adorable.
Though I probably didn't look much better myself...
I could feel my heartbeat raging out of control in my chest.
Neither of us said a word. We just looked at each other's equally disheveled state, and then, as if by silent agreement, burst out laughing.
And so, naturally, we kissed again.
The second time was still clumsy, but no longer panicked.
When her lips finally withdrew, a faint sweetness lingered on the tip of my tongue.
like a lone boat long adrift finally finding a harbor to moor at.
「We're... official now, so... we can keep going.」
「Don't you want to take some time to settle into it?」
「Hehe, I'm a speedrunner. I already picked out the kids' names just now.」
「Besides, you're still injured. Your elbow is bleeding.」
「So what—there's plenty more where that came from later.」
I sealed her mouth with mine.
The only sounds left in the room were the rustle of clothes,
and the two of us pulling apart mid-kiss to gasp for air.
The kisses that followed carried no more declaration or confirmation—
just a simple exploration of each other, straining to meet, to merge.
The world shrank very, very small,
down to just this corner of a dim room...
The room was bigger than the capsule hotel,
and yet my eyes had room for her alone.
She seemed about to say something, but didn't.
「Actually... for a while, I lived completely carefree.」
「I could tell... you died once, and it put things in perspective.」
「So when the fire broke out in the neighborhood the other day, I wasn't scared at all.」
「Because... I realized if I died, I might never see you again.」
「I... I even mocked my best friend before, the one who was going to share an apartment with me. Called her love-brained...」
「And now I've turned into the same thing... so humiliating.」
「Well then, shall I embarrass you a little more?」
Honestly, I would have been gentle even without her asking.
It's just that my own heart wasn't so steady either.
Lying flat, not caring about anything...
and yet I still wondered: what if I didn't perform well?
Would I hurt her? Would she find me off-putting?
But after several rounds of utterly untechnical, laughably clumsy "engagements"...
I found there really wasn't that much to worry about.
This wasn't a place where anyone had to win or lose.
...Or rather, who won or lost didn't matter in the slightest.
Every "probe" and "advance" was met with gentle acceptance.
And so the last sliver of distance between us disappeared.
Like two capsule shells that had drifted alone for so long,
clicking together, at just the right angle, with a snap.
From then on, the world split in two.
Divided into "us" and "everything outside of us."
from that day forward, she and I would be wrapped together inside one sweet little capsule, for the rest of our lives.
I caught up on sleep, but didn't sleep well.
After all, it was my last night in the Capsule, so my feelings were a little complicated.
One half-worn hiking pack plus a canvas bag.
Whatever else couldn't come along, I'd just leave behind.
Actually, the date I'd agreed on with the landlady was still two days off, but I decided to leave early.
Train tickets home were hard to snag, and the high-speed rail was too expensive,
so I'd let the ticket decide when I left—and it saved the cost of finding a short-term rental at the last minute.
I straightened up and looked around the Capsule I'd nearly gotten used to,
and my gaze finally settled on the bunk beside mine.
She lay on her side facing me, lips slightly parted.
She slept without a shred of wariness, sprawled out with a kind of careless boldness…
That relaxed figure was worlds away from the fragile, trembling girl she'd been before.
I'd seen this scene plenty of times before.
If I let myself look a little longer,
I had to admit she really was a cute girl.
Even her most ridiculous, most off-the-wall moments were adorable…
This was probably the last time I'd get to watch her like this. Part of me hated to let it go.
Before leaving, should I wake her and say something?
Too deliberate. It'd feel like some farewell ceremony.
It wasn't like we'd never see each other again—
we'd just be sleeping in different places, that's all.
Friends stay friends. As long as our phones had signal, nothing much would change.
At most, I'd lose the sight of her sleeping, the sounds of her washing up,
and the excited look on her face when she opened a mystery parcel. That's all.
Someday when I came back to visit, I'd ask her out for a meal,
and let her grumble a bit—"Hu Lai, you sure bolted fast back then." That would do.
Onto a new capsule, to keep living my lying-flat life.
「Are you free? I'd like to see you.」

「Whenever Lai wants to see me, I'm free!!」

「Hehe, is Lai negotiating terms with me?」
「But this isn't a few years ago anymore. What we can offer you now would shock you!」
「Doesn't matter. Don't talk compensation with a guy who's lying flat.」
「You could never truly lie flat. Maybe you don't care whether you win or lose, but you care about other people.」
「Your heart's too soft. You're always worrying about others and can't let go. That's why you helped me back then—but honestly, you're not cut out for business.」
「But that's exactly what I love about you! And exactly what I need most from you!」
「…I was wrong before. I didn't put you in the right position, and it made you miserable.」
「But now I've figured it out—I've prepared the perfect position for you too!」
「Lai, we may be loudly hyping competition and selling anxiety right now, but everyone inside the industry knows this model is played out.」
「The future is an era of hardening class lines. The returns on the rat race for ordinary people keep shrinking, and the misery keeps growing.」
「What you did… lying flat, that's what most people are choosing.」
「In an era like this, education for the masses will only get thinner and thinner on profit.」

「You wouldn't be responsible for too many people—just a select few. And you wouldn't need to feel any guilt.」
「Just carefully guide a handful of top-tier children.」
「—Unlock their potential, make their dreams come true! That's the field where you fit best, Lai.」
「Your talent and your sense of duty belong there—not to be burned up on children who are doomed to fail.」
「There's no such thing as a child who's doomed to fail…」
「And this… select few you mention—who are they?」
「The top 0.1%, or even 0.001%—high-net-worth families, of course.」
「The richer and more powerful people are, the less they can accept mediocre children.」
「Lai, you understand people's hearts—you know how to motivate and guide. With you on board, our pivot is sure to succeed!」

「And if you didn't need to pivot—would you still need me?」
「O-of course I would… because I love Lai the most!」
「And if I don't like your new business, if I don't want to help—would you still love me?」

「You did nothing wrong back then. We disagreed, and laying me off was completely correct.」
「As for you selling anxiety afterward—I don't like it… but the company needed profits.」
「Honestly, before coming here I was still hesitating. I was a little worried about you, about everyone.」
「But seeing how you all are now, my worry seems pointless…」
「With you leading them, everyone can surely keep on winning—though it has nothing to do with me.」
「When our paths diverge, there's nothing to plan together.」
「I'll go find the people who truly need me. You… don't need to trouble yourself over me anymore.」
「Lai… you're sulking again. Just like years ago.」
「People need to sulk once in a while… but I won't sulk at you people anymore.」
「I can't help you. With your resources now, you can find people many times better than me.」
「I hope you find them… anyway, good luck.」
「So you're going to keep lying flat? As a show for me?」
「Just to prove to everyone—that you didn't lose to me, that you had another choice?!」
「That's why I came today to admit defeat.」
「The path you chose was right. What I insisted on was wrong—at least for the company.」
「It's just… you winning doesn't mean I have to do what you say.」
「Admitting you're stronger than me doesn't mean I want to follow you around.」
「And you being right where I was wrong doesn't mean I have to change… what's wrong for you isn't necessarily wrong for someone else.」
「Until a few months ago, when I ran into a silly girl…」
「Boss! Have you seen Hu Lai? The kind of tall guy—the one who's always with me!」
「That girl is something else… cheery every single day, never worries about anything.」
「Terrible at games but loves them anyway. Gets flattened a hundred times, and still dares to come back for another challenge.」
「But when she loses, she never rages or sulks. At most she'll say—oopsy, died again—and go right back in.」
「She's curious about everything, wants to try everything…」
「She knows full well she's not cut out for something, and when she flops she just laughs it off and goes off to tinker with something else.」
「People look down on her, and some push her around. But the nasty words and awful stuff never seem to touch her heart at all…」
「At first I couldn't figure it out. How careless do you have to be—or how strong inside—to live like that?」
「Only later did I learn… she works at a funeral home.」
「She nearly died once, so now she's interested in everything.」
「She stands on the border between life and death, watching different people get placed into boxes every day…」
「Compared to that, what's losing a game, a little embarrassment, some gossip, a bit of contempt?」
「Next to her, the rest of us are like clowns.」
「You were right—my lying flat was just sulking, just acting out… incredibly childish.」
「But because of her, I've thought it through… admitting defeat now and then is no big deal.」
「You admit you were wrong, admit you were right; then go do what you find meaningful, or what you ought to do.」
「That's why I came to tell you all this clearly…」
「When you talk about her, there's light in your eyes.」
「I think I really have fallen in love with her.」
「You've gotten yourself all wet. Shall I get you a towel?」
Some kind of accident seemed to have happened—
there was a commotion from a table behind us, but it didn't reach this side.
The Big Boss in front of me was extremely sharp—
she noticed details even I hadn't noticed myself.
And of course… I also knew she wasn't someone who gave up easily.
「Can't help it. I love you, Lai—of course I'd get jealous. That's exactly why I wanted you back.」
Pushing open the café's glass door,
the slightly stifling heat mixed with the roar of the street hit me in the face.
Out of nowhere, a smile crept onto my lips.
It wasn't happiness or joy—just relief…
The thing that had been clogging my chest was finally removed, by my own hand.
Was it a shame? Of course it was.
These were the people I'd once grown up alongside, companions I'd cared about.
But still… everyone has to walk their own road.
Along the way, admitting you were childish, admitting you chose the wrong path,
even admitting you trusted the wrong person… it's no big deal.
What's left is to digest it all properly,
and then honestly go looking for what you truly want.
At that thought, Xiaoqi's carefree, grinning face popped into my mind.
Given the chance, I really should thank her properly…
Too bad rush hour was coming in a little while.
The train station was a fair distance away, and once quitting time hit,
the subway would be packed like a can of Spam, and a taxi would just sit in traffic.
Out of habit I pulled out my phone, but the screen stayed pitch black—
pressing the power button a few times got no response.
Guess I'd overthought things last night… and forgot to charge it.
After lying flat for so long, with no need to reply to messages right away, I'd lost my battery anxiety too… the price being I constantly forget to charge it.
My power bank was an old model that wouldn't clear security, and I hadn't brought it anyway.
I'd quit tutoring anyway, and with my personality I wasn't fit to be a teacher again.
…Nothing urgent back home that needed contacting, either.
Off the grid, out of contact—some peace and quiet for once.
As for Xiaoqi… I'd explain things to her slowly later.
The next few hours belonged entirely to me—a good chance to think things through on the train.
Think about the future, about how to plan the rest of my life…
「What do I do! What do I do! Was-was he joking? Or serious!?」

「Hu Lai must have gone to the high-speed rail station—but he'd have bought the regular bullet train ticket to save money.」
「That train leaves at seven. You have an hour and a half—if you can squeeze onto the rush-hour subway.」
「Thank you! Thank you! Thank you so much!!」
「You're my savior! Someday I'll definitely repay you!」
The train station was bustling, announcements droning overhead.
But since it was a workday,
the crowd here wasn't nearly as dense as in the subway.
Suddenly I felt no need to head in so early—better to stand outside a while longer.
My dead phone was a bit of a hassle.
I couldn't scan to pay for a bottle of water, and a lot of convenience stores can't be bothered with cash.
Might as well tough it out and deal with it once I'm home.
My thoughts inevitably drifted to her.
I'd already admitted I was "in love with her," so there was nothing to be embarrassed about.
I really did like her. Being around her was easy.
But liking her didn't mean we had to be bound together.
Running on different tracks, that stretch where our paths crossed was already an accident.
Love can also be a kind of distant admiration—
the peace of mind that comes from knowing she's living happily somewhere out there.
At that thought, I chuckled to myself a few times.
If I'd told her earlier that I was leaving, how would she have reacted?
Would she have run over to see me off, eyes red, tugging at my sleeve? Or thrown a full-on tantrum to keep me from going?
Or would she have acted like nothing happened, grinning and saying "you owe me a meal"?
Parting with such an unpredictable girl did leave some regret.
But life is full of regrets—one more won't make a difference.
The loudspeaker announced that my train was apparently boarding now.
I let out a breath, pressed down the last of those nameless feelings, and hurried into the boarding line.
It wasn't travel season, so few passengers rode this train.
I watched the scenery roll by outside the window, mentally sorting out my plans for after I got back.
First visit Mom and Dad, keep Grandma company, then do absolutely nothing—completely zone out for a week or two.
After that, I could look for other opportunities.
Someone had invited me to help build an education website—the direction actually suited me;
and a friend doing self-media wanted me to join up… all worth considering.
But the core hadn't changed: I had to carry through the essence of "lying flat"—subtraction.
Life always involves trade-offs. Too much you can't let go of, and lying flat becomes impossible.
Luckily I had no debts and few wants—plenty of time to think slowly and adjust.
On that count, I really should learn from that girl.
Be a little more "carefree," stop taking everything so seriously.
When I got home, the sky was already fully dark.
Mom and Dad didn't give me any rapturous welcome.
They just smiled faintly, asked if I'd eaten, and whether I wanted some noodles.
Seeing me come home, they didn't ask much.
Because I still hadn't told them:
why I'd come back, or when I'd be leaving again.
Actually, our relationship wasn't bad—we could at least understand each other.
Mom loved to nag, but never forced me to do things her way.
They were swamped with their business and had no time to look after me.
As a child I was raised by Grandma, and I didn't talk with them much.
I knew running a business wasn't easy for them, and even though they didn't earn much,
it was because they worked themselves to the bone that I never lacked food or clothes.
So I was always a good kid who studied hard, never giving my parents anything to worry about.
They were exhausted from hustling out there—I didn't want to add to their troubles.
And they knew they had no time to manage me, so they didn't want to pile pressure on.
they had no grounds to interfere with my life.
So, seen from outside… our relationship seemed a bit distant.
Even knowing they loved me, and I loved them…
there was a very delicate sense of distance between us.
Our family didn't have that… tell-each-other-everything atmosphere common to "ordinary families."
Much less would we do what some parents do—forcefully meddle in their child's life.
Though that kind of "meddling" is something many people hate,
and a major source of "dysfunctional family" tragedies.
But… occasionally, I had fantasized about it.
What if I'd grown up in a family like that—
parents who made a fuss over things, and the occasional quarrel with them…
Would life… have been a bit more interesting?
I'd never once made them worry,
so I had no idea how much they expected of me.
If I'd disappointed them, I didn't know whether they'd be angry.
would they… start caring about me more?
It's just a pity they were getting old…
I didn't dare try it, and I didn't want to make trouble for them.
The moment my phone charged up and booted, a stream of notifications flashed past.
Opening WeChat, 99+ unread messages had taken over the notification bar.
…I didn't need to guess who they were from.
Uneasy, I tapped her avatar and called… no answer.
Switching to the contacts page, I dialed her number… the phone was off.
Of course she would be. I'd just up and left without a word.
Even if we were only roommates, I at least owed her a proper goodbye…
A little guilty, and a little uneasy.
I picked up the phone again and opened WeChat, staring at her hundreds of messages,
especially the run of voice messages at the end… I couldn't quite bring myself to play them.
Then, just as I was composing a reply—
「Where-wh-where's your home!? I can't find it! I just can't—」
「Give me back my phone! What are you doing!」
Sounds of chaos came through the line.
「Sorry, sorry! Just two more words! Only two!」
「—Give it back or I'm calling the police!」
Then it hit me—the caller ID just now… was a local number.
So I grabbed my jacket and ran out the door,
with no time to explain to my parents, who were still cooking noodles.
That was probably the fastest, most desperate run of my entire life.
The cold wind drove off my drowsiness, my brain racing at full speed,
yet a smile hung on my lips—
「So sorry, so sorry for the trouble.」
「…Lunatic. Who grabs someone's phone in the middle of the street!」
Across from me was a stern-faced older man—
I'd reached him midway and gotten their location.
Though he'd been fuming at first,
after I pressed two packs of cigarettes on him, his face quickly softened.
「Couple's quarrel… don't make trouble for society.」
「Right, you're absolutely right, sir! We'll be careful from now on!」
The man wanted to say more, but he glanced at the girl who'd snatched his phone, then at me, gave a wry chuckle, and left.
Then, on the empty small-town street,
only the sound of two people breathing remained.
…Unable to bear it, I turned my head to the side.
She was very close to me.
Close enough that I could see the beads of sweat on her forehead,
her slightly disheveled hair swaying slowly as her head drooped—
When she lifted her head, her face was like an overturned palette:
excitement, joy, the grievances of the long chase, and an unmistakable trace of resentment.
making her expression too complicated for me to read at first.
That feeling of having a mountain of things to say,
but no idea where to start—I felt exactly the same.
"What are you doing, chasing me to my hometown?"
"I'm sorry. I should have told you before I left."
"Why'd you grab someone else's phone? Where's yours?"
"Are you okay? Your knees are all scraped up."
Things like that—I wanted to say them all in one breath.
But I didn't know which to say first…
And so, at the end of that strange silence.
「Hubby doesn't want me anymore—hubby doesn't want me anymore—」
「I-I just went home for a bit…」
「You dumped me and ran—you didn't answer my calls, you didn't reply to my messages—」
「I forgot to charge my phone! It wasn't on purpose!」
「I chased you all the way to the station—I watched you get on the train—I couldn't catch up at all—」
「I got off the train and couldn't find you—then I got lost running around—and my phone died too—」
She was babbling, breathing so hard she could barely get air. I quickly steadied her.
「Don't rush. Calm down first. Deep breaths… tell me slowly.」
As if following my instructions, she sucked in a sharp breath, then let it out heavily.
But her color didn't seem to improve at all.
Then, she slowly lowered her head,
and revealed a slightly silly smile, full of enormous relief.
「I ran too fast… it was kilometers… my head's a little dizzy…」

「Who'd dare stay around you when you're half-dead like this?」
Looking the way she did, if she played dead one more time, I'd definitely have believed it...
「Comfort me a little... I feel awful...」
「How about you get some proper sleep first?」
「That's enough, isn't it? It's really hot out...」
「Ten more seconds of hugging... Ten, nine, eight...」
「You're counting way too slowly. Time's up—go to sleep.」
「Sleep in your own bed. Why are you draped over me?」
「I'll be in the living room. Change into your pajamas and get some real sleep...」
「Oh, right—the weather's been dry lately, and the wiring in these old buildings is mostly past its prime.」
「We'll probably need the air conditioning too. For the sake of the circuits—fire safety—let's not use the induction stove.」
「For meals, we can order delivery, or go out to eat?」
There she was, utterly defenseless as always,
still wearing that oversized T-shirt of mine.
Setting aside that scatterbrained, pestering personality of hers...
asleep, she really was a cute, attractive girl.
Someone else might have enjoyed the nice view.
Unfortunately, I wasn't in the mood...
Ever since the day I told her the hotel was on its last legs, she hadn't been sleeping properly.
During the day she forced herself to stay upbeat...
hovering around in front of me, finding excuses to chat.
I knew she was a little reluctant to let go.
Reluctant to leave this cramped, shabby "double room" that barely kept out the wind and rain—and her temporary roommate, me.
「What's the plan after this?! Where will you live? Still nearby?」
「I'll figure it out as I go. I'm a lie-flat guy, after all. No rush.」
「Then I'm following you! Wherever you go, I go!」
「Isn't your work nearby? You need to find a place close to it.」
「Who cares if the commute's longer? I don't care—I'm living with you!」
「And what if I go back to my hometown, or move to another city?」
「The rent pressure around here is heavy, after all... Why else would I be living in a capsule hotel?」
「...We're still friends on WeChat. It's not like we're cutting ties. What's there to be afraid of?」
「It's not the same... Having a game shut off halfway through—that hurts.」
「Either way... I'll come find you! And if I can't find you right away, we'll just call it absence making the heart grow fonder! Maybe after some time apart, I'll love you even more!」
She looked like she was about to cry... She probably wasn't joking.
She was a girl who wore her heart on her sleeve—natural enough that she'd hate to part,
She's probably like this with everyone.
Honestly, I was a little reluctant too.
To tell the truth, hanging around with her was pretty easy.
A guy and a girl living together is a bit odd...
But being around her took no effort—I didn't have to worry about saying the wrong thing.
Watching her carefree antics now and then even let me breathe a little, too.
With her temperament, everything just rolls off her back,
she doesn't hold grudges, and nobody can easily push her around.
There was no need for me to worry about her...
So I'd just keep things with her at this distance—not too far, not too close. Even apart, we could stay in touch.
We could keep chatting online. I'd snap a photo of anything fun or tasty and send it her way,
and every so often we could meet up for a meal. That's about all it would be.
It's not that I never had the chance to get closer.
It's not that I didn't want to get closer...
we could have been closer, more intimate, and I could have understood her better.
But I felt... there was no need.
The essence of lying flat is quitting the whole "win or lose" system
and finding the life you like, the life that suits you.
But there are two problems that are very hard to overcome...
First: you can only keep yourself in check. You can't talk anyone else into lying flat.
it's very hard to sincerely, wholeheartedly let the people you care about lie flat.
but you can't let the people you care about lose along with you.
That's why so many parents want to lie flat themselves, to take it easy and stay Zen,
yet in the end they dutifully sign their kids up for cram schools.
So "lying flat" is very hard to carry through.
If you want to truly lie flat,
you not only have to let yourself go—you have to learn to let others go too.
A surplus sense of responsibility is meaningless, especially for someone like me—
limited in ability, unable to help people much, unable to take charge of their futures.
So... better to keep my distance from the start.
Don't step into other people's lives; don't let them step into mine. Better for everyone.
Either way, the "capsule hotel" days were numbered.
Meeting a live wire like Xiaoqi
just as those days were winding down was an unexpected bonus.
A few days ago the landlady sighed and moaned at me for ages.
Said the authorities had ordered her to make rectifications, with a whole list of fire-safety problems.
But lately it's been hot and dry, plus peak season for electricity use—
I've lost count of the fire trucks I've seen on the streets...
So the authorities' concern wasn't unreasonable.
Honestly, running a capsule hotel in this neighborhood was reckless to begin with...
The building was older than me, its tangled wiring impossible to sort out,
and the surrounding roads were so narrow a fire truck couldn't get in at all.
If a fire really broke out one day, even running for it wouldn't be easy...
Whatever. Not thinking about that now.
I'd go to the library and return all my borrowed books—it'd make moving easier in a few days.
Tonight, when Xiaoqi woke up, I'd help her pack.
Knowing her, she probably hadn't even started looking for a new place...
It was dark, and she hadn't replied to any of the messages I'd sent.
For a night shift, she should have been awake by now.
But she hadn't been sleeping well lately—maybe she was still catching up.
I needed to get back and wake her up...
A crowd had gathered over there, all noise and commotion.
Several fire trucks, blindingly red, were jammed at the narrow entrance to the complex.
Their warning lights flickered bright and dark across the faces of the crowd.
Firefighters in heavy gear dragged hoses as they ran inside...
Voices and sirens blended into one roar.
From the chatter beside me, I gathered that a unit inside had caught fire,
but the road was too narrow for the trucks—they had to run hose lines instead.
「My child! My child is still upstairs!」
「Stay calm! The fire's under control—our people are already up there! Going in now will only get in the way!」
I stood on tiptoe, but all I could see was a sea of heads. No flames.
One building blocked my line of sight—I couldn't see the hotel's building at all.
It's not ours, right? Unless it's the hotel that caught fire!?
Outlets, plugs, unplugging the water heater the moment we were done—careful as could be.
But in an old building, fire spreads fast. There was no telling how it could go.
I keep my valuables on me,
and the rest isn't worth anything. If it burns, it burns.
I messaged her again, but every text vanished like a stone in the sea.
She should have been awake by now...
If something had really happened, knowing her, she'd have blasted me with messages by now...
The firefighters are here. It's fine.
She was probably just sleeping like the dead—nothing wakes her up...
Under cover of the chaos and the dark, I plunged back into that familiar run-down building.
lit only by the sickly green glow of emergency lamps on the wet floor.
They must have cut this building's power for safety.
I ran fast, my footsteps echoing through the empty stairwell.
The smell of smoke in here was faint... which calmed me a little.
No firefighters on this side—their voices were concentrated in the next building over...
So it was the building next door that had caught fire.
The water on the floor must have splashed over while they were putting it out...
Looks like our building was safe for now.
But these crummy buildings stood too close together—there was no guarantee the fire wouldn't spread.
And the smoke in the stairwell was getting thicker. Getting out immediately was definitely the right call.
—And that idiot was still sound asleep!
By the time I burst into our familiar capsule room, the smell of smoke was unmistakable.
My throat tightened. I started calling her name.
Until I saw her behind the curtain, lying on her bunk,
motionless, the blanket wrapped around her in a ball.
「Holy crap, don't scare me like that! Still sleeping?!」
「You never pull the curtain, and you pick now to pull it?!」
The moment I touched her shoulder...
I felt warmth, and a faint trembling.
I collapsed onto the floor on the spot.
Only then did the cold sweat belatedly break out.
I caught my breath, wanting to curse her out.
But the words turned into a stream of nagging the moment they left my mouth—
maybe to steady my own pounding heart.
「What are you doing!? Playing a corpse again!?」
「The building next door is on fire, you know that? At least check the occasion before joking around!」
「This firetrap would go up at the first spark, and there isn't even a proper emergency exit!」
「—When trouble shows up, you run! Immediately!」
「Enough, get up! We have to leave right now!」
I went on and on, losing my composure.
But my words were like pebbles thrown into a deep pond—not even an echo came back.
She just lay curled up there, not moving.
She pulled pranks, sure—but not at a time like this, not like this...
I moved closer and gently laid a hand on her shoulder.
At my touch, her body flinched violently,
curling up even tighter, as if scalded.
A trembling beyond her control—faint yet fierce,
enough to make the flimsy bunk creak softly.
She had wedged herself into the gap between the blanket and the capsule wall,
leaving me nothing but a thin figure braced against the whole world.
No wonder she'd been so hesitant around the gas stove before.
But... this was way beyond that.
I tried to keep my voice as steady as I could, like soothing a child.
「We have to leave now. The building isn't safe yet.」
She didn't answer, and she didn't turn around.
Only that trembling she couldn't suppress
came through the hand I kept on her shoulder.
After a long while, just as I'd decided she wasn't going to respond,
the curled-up back gave the smallest nod.
I was silent for a few seconds. This wouldn't do.
I bent down, moving as gently as I could.
One arm slipped under her knees, the other carefully around her back.
My voice was barely there, like coaxing a frightened child.
Then, slowly gathering my strength, I lifted her out of that narrow bunk.
She was so light—light as a leaf, as if she'd crumple at the gentlest fold.
She was still trembling, but she didn't resist.
I shifted her onto my back.
Her arms looped around my neck without thinking, her face buried behind my shoulder.
I didn't dare speak again, nor did I deliberately try to look at her face.
Once outside, I didn't dare walk fast. I just carried her,
step by step, down the dim stairwell thick with the smell of scorching.
「You two okay? What happened to her?」
「She's fine... Twisted her ankle. I'm carrying her out.」
The firefighter didn't press further—the fire was already under control.
But the crowd of onlookers hadn't dispersed. The residents held back outside buzzed with talk,
guessing at the cause of the fire, loudly denouncing something or other...
I didn't listen closely, because the breathing against my back was still a little ragged.
I carried her all the way to the riverbank.
I picked a corner with few people around.
Here there was only the sound of the wind and the river flowing.
The city's distant din and the chaos we'd just left were shut out.
The wind blew damp against our faces,
chilly enough to clear my head a little.
I found a dry spot and slowly set her down,
propping her against the stone steps of the embankment.
She lifted her head, her body still trembling faintly.
I wanted to ask if she felt better, but seeing her like that... better to wait.
So I held back the urge to keep asking questions.
I swallowed every line like "this isn't like you," "what happened all of a sudden," "did something happen before"—swallowed them all back down.
All I could do was stand up and take out my phone
to check the residents' group chat for updates.
Xiaoqi suddenly flung herself at me.
I froze, my arms hanging in midair with nowhere to go.
She was trying to stuff her whole self into my arms,
burying her head desperately into the crook of my neck.
like a terrified little animal searching for a safe corner.
That familiar scent, faintly of body wash,
mixed with her panicked breath and swallowed me whole.
Her hands clutched the clothes at my back, the fabric pulled taut,
her fingertips pressing through the thin T-shirt almost into my skin.
As if she still didn't feel close enough,
she kept trying, futilely and ceaselessly, to squeeze herself further in.
My first reflex was that this probably wasn't proper—I should push her away.
But it also felt... under the circumstances, pushing her away would be a little cruel.
Her fragility passed through her skin to mine with nothing in between.
...I felt like I should hold her.
But how does one hold someone?
I was flustered... more flustered than when I'd charged into the fire just now.
How much pressure, at what angle?
As who? In what frame of mind? With what purpose, would I hold her?
Once I held her, would a lot of things be completely different?
And so the two of us stayed frozen—her burrowing with all her might, my hands hovering in the air—
like a couple of clumsy lovebirds closing in for the first time,
groping in the dark for a position to warm each other.
A gust of river wind swept over without warning, carrying a thread of chill.
Yes, yes... I was keeping her warm.
Holding her was only so she wouldn't catch cold.
Just for warmth. Nothing else meant by it.
The excuse was self-deception, but at least it was usable... So be it, then.
My hovering arms finally came down,
gently, with a trace of hesitation, tightening around her.
so her cheek rested more snugly against my chest.
My palm, somewhat clumsily, patted her back, one beat at a time.
And the trembling in my arms gradually subsided.
Her body was so soft, like a kitten that had just slipped indoors to safety,
leaning against me... with a trust that held nothing back.
That girlish breath, pure and fragile,
seeped through every exhale, through our touching skin... straight into my heart.
A string in my heart had been plucked...
Truthfully, it had been plucked long ago.
Only today was I willing to admit it.
Even as I kept telling myself
that I was only comforting a frightened child,
sliding through her fine, soft hair, gently stroking it, again and again.
the river wind, the night, the blurry lights in the distance all faded into a mere backdrop.
The posture of this embrace, the gentle breathing,
and the mingled warmth and scent of us brought a peace beyond words.
As if we had lived like this for years already,
long since used to each other's presence.
Like an old married couple, grown children and all,
nestled by the river, reminiscing about the years gone by.
...Even though we'd known each other for barely a few months.
