The ball clanged off the back rim and bounced away.
Frowning, I walked over to pick it up, resigned.
Seventh spot, third miss of the day.
but muscle memory should be more reliable than this.
Looks like my mood's been a bit restless lately...
This was an old basketball court, its facilities worn, but it was free.
On weekday days the square-dancing aunties occupied it,
so weekend afternoons were actually a little less crowded.
Basketball was one of my few hobbies,
and for a guy who's lying flat, the sport is convenient too.
It keeps up basic fitness and loosens joints stiff from sitting.
Compared with plain long-distance running, it works more of the body.
Occasionally you'd run into a few similarly quiet people who just wanted to sweat, and you could piece together a pickup game.
Nobody knew each other, and nobody bothered to,
so win or lose, it didn't matter, and nobody took it seriously.
Keep the mind calm, and the shots fall naturally.
「Good grief, this place is impossible to find! What a maze!」
「That's exactly why hardly anyone comes here...」
「So why did you come running over? Didn't you say you were doing a murder-mystery game with friends this afternoon?」
「Don't get me started! Everyone bailed! One said her boyfriend was visiting, one said her cat got sick!」
「And the last one was the most ridiculous—the sun's too strong, she's afraid of getting tan! I'm furious!」
「Ah. Well, you could go home and sleep, or find something else to do.」
「Going back would be so boring. Observing Hu Lai's lying-flat daily life might be more fun than a murder-mystery game.」
「Is there a problem with me playing basketball?」
「A lie-flat guy and sports don't go together, you know~」
「Lying flat means doing whatever you feel like doing. I like basketball, so I play.」
「Your shooting form is so textbook! So cool!」
「The jump, the lift, the snap of the wrist—one smooth motion.」
「You know this stuff? Have you played?」
「Never touched a basketball, but I was on the cheer squad in college, so I watched the players all the time.」
「You've got... kind of a pro vibe, you know.」
「Do anything enough times and it looks like that. Nothing special.」
「Hey, why are you staring at me!」
「Just observing... now that I look closely, have you always been this fit?」
「Before I just thought you were tall, but seeing you move—your muscle definition is so defined. Kind of sexy.」
「Ooh, he's blushing! His ears are burning!」
「Oh, right, right! Can you teach me? I want to learn to shoot! That, that form you just did!」
「Come on, what's the harm in teaching me! I'm not dumb!」
「So stingy. Fine, I'll just watch from the side, and every time you miss I'll heckle you.」
But for all her talk, in the end she just watched quietly.
She might seem clueless about what's good for her... but actually she had good manners.
Not that I could practice much longer anyway—people would start showing up soon.
Before long, a few boys and girls with basketballs trickled onto the court,
probably middle schoolers from the neighborhood.
They stood timidly at the other half court and started trying to shoot.
Their form was terribly raw—some threw like shot-putters, others lofted shots flat as cannonballs.
「There's a PE test tomorrow, and none of us are any good.」
「They still test this in PE class?」

「In a lot of places the PE section of the high school entrance exam has elective items, like dribble layups or spot shooting. Even where it doesn't count for the exam, regular tests might include it.」
「Yeah, the teacher said it counts toward our final grade...」
「Your form is off. You snap the wrist like this—you don't push with your arms.」
「The power starts from your feet and travels up to your hands. See? Mostly from here—」
「Hold the ball above your forehead, not behind your head or in front of your face.」
「Playing favorites. You teach them but not me...」
「They have a test—that's real business. You just want to play.」
「Playing is real business too! I happen to be free.」
「If you're free, how about helping fetch the balls?」
She refused out loud, but her hands and feet were plenty diligent.
Her steps dragged a bit reluctantly at first.
As she bent to pick up a ball, her long hair slid off her shoulder like a soft waterfall, nearly brushing the ground.
She casually tucked it behind an ear with her fingers and gathered up the dusty basketball.
After tossing the ball back, she seemed to discover some fun in it and got into the groove.
Another shot went wide and thumped away toward the far side...
This time she chased it down and flicked it to a stop with her foot,
then scooped it up, grinning goofily as if she'd cracked the trick.
Finding joy even in fetching balls... what a strange girl.
「Remember the key points, keep practicing to build the feel, and don't get nervous during the test.」
Let them practice on their own; from here on it's just about putting in the hours.
「What now? What are you sulking about?」
「Isn't it my turn for some of your time now?」
「So warm to strangers, so cold to people you know. Marrying you would be such a loss...」
「Can you stop leaping around topics like that? I'm going back to practice... You can fetch balls if you're bored.」
「You don't have to. I'll manage on my own.」
「Boss! There's an open spot over here!」
Over came a group of taller young guys in matching tank tops—students from a nearby university, probably.
The one in front swept his eyes over the court and landed on the middle schoolers practicing their shots.
「Move it, kids! We're using this court.」
The middle schoolers froze, hugging their balls, looking scared... then instinctively glanced at me.
「Guys, these kids have a shooting test in PE tomorrow. They still need to practice a while.」
「There are two hoops here. How about each group takes one side?」
「We've got a game tomorrow. We need to run tactical drills, full court.」
「They're just shooting around. They won't get in your way.」
「What if they get bumped? You gonna take responsibility for injuries?」
「A basketball test for middle schoolers... just find any old spot and chuck up a few shots, done.」
「The court is public. Let's all share it.」
「Have some decency, okay! First come, first served—who just shoves people off a court?」
「Miss, we really do have a game tomorrow.」
「The school gym got taken by the starters...」
「I—I'm the first-string small forward! I'm a sub for tactical reasons!」
「Right... being a sub has nothing to do with skill. It's the coach's call.」
「Your training matters, sure, but the kids' test is legitimate business too... How about letting them practice for half an hour?」
The guy gave me a few unfriendly once-overs.
Probably stoked by that silly girl, he couldn't back down now.
Judging by the look of him, he wasn't going to just let this go...
「Streetball has streetball rules. All that talk is useless. Let's go one-on-one!」
「Just you and me. You win, the court's all yours. You lose, you take the kids and your girl and get lost!」
「Come on, boss, don't bully an amateur.」
「Yeah, we are the school team, after all.」
「True... I'm not much of a player. What's there to compete over?」
「We'll play ten baskets. I won't even ask you to win. Just score one basket against me—」
「Just one! And you win. The court's yours today. How's that? Generous, right?」
「How about this: if by some fluke I score one, you give the kids twenty minutes of practice time. Deal?」
「Hmph. I'm not going all out against an amateur.」
Sigh. Another meaningless contest of winning and losing.
This guy was good... first-string small forward probably wasn't just talk.
Maybe he was worked up, or maybe he wanted to show off in front of a pretty girl, but he came in hot.
His physical tools were genuinely strong—explosiveness and speed far beyond an ordinary person's...
He'd scored three baskets in the blink of an eye. Not easy to guard.
「Buddy, you need to work out more! No core strength. You've gotta play like me!」
I'd let him score seven now. Close enough.
Couldn't lose too embarrassingly—scoring one would be a decent gesture.
Best not to bruise the guy's ego... He was young and hot-blooded. Not worth it.
From a fair distance from him,
I jumped backward for a shot and then accidentally tumbled to the ground.
The ball traced a high, floaty arc through the air with no aesthetic merit whatsoever.
Finally it clanked off the front rim and, under everyone's gaze,
rattled and wobbled its way down through the hoop.
「Hahaha, buddy, what kind of form was that?」
I was sitting on the ground at that moment, a living demonstration of the total failure of the "fadeaway."
A performance that pathetic shouldn't raise anyone's suspicions.
「Thank you for going easy on me. Pure luck, really.」
「Your leaping ability is amazing. To get away from your defense I had to gamble like that...」
The lead small forward looked like he'd swallowed a fly.
But since it was pure dumb luck on my part, he hadn't exactly lost face.
The guy waved his arm in sour, humiliated frustration,
and herded his teammates to the other end of the court.
His temper definitely hadn't been vented... but the matter was settled perfectly.
「What was that last shot? So ugly.」
「...What does it matter how I shot it? It went in.」
「Your shooting form was so pretty earlier. You made yourself look bad on purpose, didn't you?」
「Come on, you don't know basketball. Guarded and unguarded are two different things—no time to look pretty.」
「No, no, of course not... not fooling you.」
「You kids keep going. Twenty minutes is plenty.」
But why she was angry, I couldn't figure out.
I'd just let her be mad for a while...
Suddenly, her gaze swept across my face like a searchlight,
then snapped toward the college guys in the distance, and whipped right back.
A familiar sense of foreboding rose in my chest.
That was the expression she wore opening mystery boxes, and just before sitting down at a computer to play CS...
—Oh no. She was about to stir something up.
She called out in a deliberately loud, coquettish voice, and then latched onto me tightly with both arms!
「Hubby, are you okay!? Did you hurt yourself when you fell just now!」
「Where did you land? Oh no, is your arm okay? Let me see your hand!」
—What on earth is this girl playing at!
「Could the old injury have flared up! Didn't the doctor say you'd fully recovered? Does it still hurt!」
「I was worried sick! Don't go so hard against amateurs, okay!」
「Let's focus on recovering, and go compete against the pros when we're back. Don't play amateurs out here, okay? Hubby?」
I didn't need to look to know
that gaze from across the court had turned into a red-hot branding iron.
The guy's chest heaved violently, teeth grinding audibly.
His buddies beside him probably couldn't hold him back anymore...
「Calm down, calm down! Buddy, take it easy!」
「Throwing the game on purpose! And letting your woman snipe at me from the sidelines?!」
「No, no, I didn't throw anything... Games have winners and losers. That was a luck shot.」
「Cut the crap! A luck shot? You think I'm blind?! And your wife! Who are you two putting on this show for?」
「You've got it all wrong, really... She's not my wife. She talks nonsense—don't take it to heart.」
「Wrong... heh! Sure, sure! Today I've been played for a complete fool!」
「You're all the same! You all think I'm trash, that I deserve to be benched, deserve to be looked down on, huh?!」
「Buddy, it's just a pickup game... And you play really well.」
「—Well, my foot! What good does playing well do?! I play well and still ride the bench! Watching those coach's favorites stroll around on court!」
「And you outsiders, you've come to stomp on me too, huh?」
「Winning one basket isn't enough—your woman has to jump in with a few extra jabs, like I don't already know my place!」
「Uh, buddy... I don't know anything about your personal situation, and I meant no offense.」
「Apologize my ass! Guys with a bit of talent putting on airs—I've seen plenty! And you, behind me—」
「Bringing along some drama-queen skank to cheer for you! Showing off how gracious and superior you are, huh?!」
「Boss... saying that is... kind of going too far...」
「Buddy. Who were you just talking about?」
「Whoever... whoever bites back, that's who I'm talking about!」
「You want an apology? Fine! We play again!」
「You win, I'll get on my knees and apologize! You lose, you two get out of here and I never want to see you again!」
Before the words finished, my body had moved ahead of my mind.
The first bounce of the dribble was low and urgent—

The undefended basket swelled rapidly in my vision.
Full-force push off the floor, a savage snap in my hands, together with the ball—

the ball was slammed viciously down through the ring.
The looks the college guys gave me changed.
I knew I was throwing down a provocation,
but at this point there was no pretending anymore.
「Damn it... you were toying with me the whole time!」

The guy caught the ball, took a deep breath, and exploded into motion.
His footwork was explosive, his crossovers fierce,
and the angle of his dipping shoulder carried menace.
At least in pure physical terms, he was very strong.
But his emotions were clearly running too hot, wrecking his focus—
Each time he tried to shoulder open space or stop-and-cut, I'd already cut him off.
Finding no way to break through, he forced a fadeaway,
and the ball clipped the side of the rim and bounded far away.
But now that he'd confirmed I was a tough customer,
the manic edge in his eyes gradually receded.
Good. He could still control his temper.
A legitimate player, not a complete hothead...
When my turn came, his defense was ferocious.
The instant I started dribbling he was right up on me,
his arms pestering me like vines.
「—Come on! Weren't you quite the jumper? Let's see you drive past me!」
The guy's fundamentals were beyond reproach. Getting past him wouldn't be easy.
One simple crossover into a between-the-legs pullback,
and the instant he instinctively shifted his weight, I rose for the shot.
He'd clearly adjusted his tactics, lowering his center of gravity, no longer charging mindlessly.
My defense stepped up accordingly—every position battle firmer, denying him any opening.
Of course, now and then I could dangle a fake opening...
He timed it and charged from the right, but I'd been ready and sealed the lane instantly.
He'd overcommitted; his shoulder slammed into my chest like a sledgehammer.

Good. At least he didn't deny it.
The game went on, but the atmosphere had changed.
Faster transitions, fierce physical battles, but clean play.
He blocked one of my mid-range shots; I swatted one of his layups.
When it came back to my offense, his defense grew even more suffocating.
His height and wingspan fully deployed, glued nearly against my body,
hands constantly harassing my sightline and dribble, footwork lightning quick.
this guy ranked top three in overall ability among people I'd faced.
Once he calmed down, his physical gifts and defensive fundamentals began to tell.
Speed, strength, reach—all above mine. He clearly had the edge now.
The feeling of squeezing out every last drop of focus to think, anticipate, and battle... wasn't bad at all.
But conquering the "challenge" in front of me
stirred an excitement I hadn't felt in a long time.
I dropped my weight, faked a drive to the left with my body, while my eyes sneaked a glance right.
He hesitated, and just as I'd predicted, slid his weight half a step to the right.
So I pounded my right foot into the ground, crossed over,
and burst through the momentary gap on the left!
His reactions were lightning fast. With a low growl he chased at full speed,
and the instant I left the ground, he leaped with everything he had.
He nearly blocked my path, but his balance was gone now—he had no power to use.
So with everything I had, I slammed the ball down toward the hoop!
The instant the ball was slammed home, I could feel him lose his balance.
The force of the collision vanished all at once,
and behind me came the heavy crash of him hitting the ground.
The guy lay on the ground, motionless,
only his chest heaving, eyes staring upward, gaze somewhat hollow.
The other college guys stood around watching him in dead silence.
I didn't celebrate, and I didn't look back again,
avoiding any eye contact as best I could.
The way he looked reminded me of students who'd failed their exams—
having given everything and still unable to win, going all-out and still falling off the list.
The guy was genuinely arrogant and obnoxious,
but he had wanted to beat me fair and square.
「I'm sorry... my mouth ran away from me. What I said was out of line.」
He walked slowly over to Xiaoqi,
and he truly meant to kneel and apologize, but I pulled him back up.
「Huh? No, no! I went a bit too far just now too... hahahaha.」
「We only need one hoop. You can keep practicing on the rest.」
「Forget it. Practice won't help... I'm just built to ride the bench.」
「Is it your defense that's keeping you out of the starting lineup?」
「You've got great physical tools—speed and strength both—and your positioning instincts are solid.」
「You just smother too close—sure, the pressure's real. But that only scares novices. Savvy players don't buy it.」
「Up that tight, you also bite on fakes—one glance and you're taken clean out of the play.」
「With your speed, you don't need to stay that tense. Give a little room, and I'd have nothing on you.」
「Besides, in a real game your teammates help on defense. Getting beaten occasionally isn't a disaster.」
「Fix those points, and whether or not you start tomorrow, the starting job will be yours sooner or later.」
「I think the coach said pretty much the same thing...」
「No. My stamina's done for the day.」
「Two more rounds and I'd definitely lose. That's not modesty.」
He said nothing more, though his eyes were complicated.
He silently waved his teammates over to the other half court,
and their practice looked far steadier than before.
「That dunk just now was insane! Can you teach us?!」
「Not much time left. Practice what's on your test first.」
「Remember, snap the wrist, bend the knees... I'm heading off.」
「Are you mad? Don't be mad, don't be mad. Weren't you just so cool out there!」
「The dunk was so cool! Wow! Just incredible!」
「Stop saying that word. Enough is enough.」
「I took the joke too far... I shouldn't have done that.」
「Really, really, I'm sorry. I went too far... I just wanted to see what you're like when you get serious.」
「I didn't expect you to be this good! Were you a pro before? You can actually dunk—testosterone overload!」
「Not a pro. I spent two years on my college team, then barely played seriously after that.」
「These past two years I've played a lot of pickup, so I've recovered some... but it's only enough to push students around.」
「If that guy got serious and we kept going, I couldn't have won. My stamina wouldn't hold up.」
「Who knows, Hu Lai my classmate, keeper of hidden depths.」
「Nothing hidden... This is all there is...」
「Hehehe, hidden or not, we'll find out soon enough.」
「No. I simply told him what I think.」
「With that cheater at the internet café, you didn't seem to have this much to say.」
「That dyed-hair guy at the café was a sore loser... This guy lost and owned it. They're not the same.」
「You're... still mad? I apologized so sincerely.」
「If you're not mad, why the long face?」
「Nothing worth being happy about happened either...」
「You're a weird one. Other people lose and get sad, but you win and look like the weight of the world's on you? So contrary.」
「Because it was already settled, and you had to go and stick your oar in.」
「I'm telling you, doing it your way might actually make the other guy angrier.」
「Think about it. You go easy in games, and you go easy on the court too.」
「If the other guy can't tell, fine. But if he's got any skill and figures it out, he'll feel like you're toying with him.」
「Like just now—if you'd come out and crushed him from the start, none of that mess afterward would've happened.」
「Winning and losing get tangled up with a lot—pride, interests, relationships...」
「So a lot of things aren't worth fighting over. Step back, and everyone breathes easier.」
「You don't get sad when you lose? Don't get jealous?」
「A loss is a loss. Admit you played badly this time, admit you're bad at it—what's the big deal?」
「And what if the other side cheats? Plays dirty?」
「Then that's his shame. It just shows he can't afford to lose. Why should I get worked up?」
「And if they win, then come preen in your face and gross you out?」
「Hahaha, that's their lack of class. What do I have to be sad about?」
「Besides, in games and matches, meeting an opponent is like opening a mystery box.」
「If you really run into a sore loser with no class, just don't play with him next time...」
「But if by chance you meet someone like you—even if I lose, I still learn something from you. That's a net gain!」
「Hmm? Why are you looking at me like that? Did I say something wrong?」
...Did she really not care about winning and losing?
If everyone thought the way she did,
the world wouldn't have half as much nonsense in it.
「You were enjoying yourself at the end too, weren't you?」
「I noticed, you know. You were smiling... at the most intense part, you were having so much fun.」
「Hahaha! I nailed it, didn't I! I knew it!」
「Hmph hm, now I know you a little bit more! Such a sense of accomplishment! Hahahaha—」
「Hey, hey, hey—stop pulling me. What are you doing?」
「I do kind of like you! But—but isn't this too fast? We should do things in order...」
「Ohhh!! It's CS! You should've said so earlier!」
「Come on, come on! Let's battle it out! I still have a score to settle with you!」
「That's what you get for standing around dumb—any common camping spot and you just walk into it!」
What followed was, essentially, a one-sided history of her "suffering."
Whatever tactics she tried—ambushes, rushes, camping—I dismantled them one by one.
Every time she thought she'd figured out the pattern and was about to succeed—
my play would subtly notch up a level,
and I'd precisely cut her down right at victory's door.
「You're definitely toying with me! Every time I think I can win, you insta-kill me!」
「In game design, it's called dynamic difficulty adjustment.」
「The opponent's strength adjusts in real time to your level. Always leaving you feeling like you're just one step from winning. Haha.」
「Dang it, so you've been looking down on me! You scheming man!」
「Guilty. I'm full of schemes. Let's see which level you can reach.」
「I don't believe it! Tonight I WILL force out your final form!」
「Late, schmate! I'm on night-shift hours anyway, I've got jet lag to fix!—Fight to the last! Slit my throat and ascend to heaven!」
The room held only game sound effects and her intermittent wails.
And I confirmed it: she genuinely did not care about winning or losing.
When she won, she cheered and jumped;
when she lost, she groaned for one second and queued up the next round.
No pride in winning, no lingering grudge in losing.
She was simply, purely, enjoying the process of "playing."
Watching the little figure on screen dart around nimbly, only to finally fall to my gun,
listening to her shout "Ahhh, so close again!" from the other end.
Some string inside me that had been involuntarily wound tight in every human interaction,
in this cramped capsule, on this deep night... quietly loosened.
So this is how you could be with people.
No calculating gains and losses, no fretting over every subtle shift in the other person's mood—
you could freely bring your full strength to the contest.
Because you knew that whatever the outcome,
the person across from you wouldn't change how they treated you because of it.
The feeling... was unfamiliar, but comfortable. Even a little luxurious.
If, a few years earlier, the person I'd met had been like this...
maybe a lot of things would have turned out differently.
「No rush. You've got plenty of deaths left.」

I push open the front door, plastic bag from the wet market in hand.
The bag holds leaf lettuce, chicken breast, peanuts and dried chilies,
plus a whole tray of eggs and a big pack of seaweed that cost a buck.
Too much to do today, so I only made it to the market this afternoon.
Go in the morning and you can at least pick fresher vegetables...
I really have been a bit busy lately.
In the morning I tutored a high schooler on leave from school,
and in the afternoon I went to a small education website and recorded two open classes.
Didn't even have time to pick my girlfriend up from work... a bit of a shame.
After a few months, I've gotten used to life in this rented room.
It's a shared apartment, but the only long-term residents are me and Xiaoqi...
Two young women moved in at one point,
but they only stayed half a month before leaving.
Most of the time, this is a little world just for the two of us.
When I'm not busy, I take her to and from work;
when things get busy, we each handle our own share.
More and more parents have been coming to me for tutoring and consulting lately.
Plenty of them are still odd, but I can handle it.
It used to feel like a hassle... now that I have motivation, I'm not so picky about the work.
I keep feeling I should save more money, to plan for the life ahead.
Honestly, Xiaoqi is a low-desire person too.
She really could stay in a rented room with me her whole life.
But... sometimes the less she cares, the more you want to give her.
People are funny like that sometimes...
The more your parents tell you to rest, that grades don't matter that much,
the more you want to do well.
「Bear hug~ bear hug~ gimme some HP back, hahahaha—」
「Careful, I'm washing vegetables, my hands are wet.」
「Wet's even better—it's got that lived-in feel!」
「Mango pomelo sago! With a coupon it's half price AND buy-one-get-one! Tonight's drinks are sorted.」
「...Nice. We can freeze whatever we don't finish.」
「Why don't you go rest a bit? Tonight it's stir-fried lettuce, kung pao chicken, and a seaweed egg-drop soup.」
「All my favorites! Hubby, you're the best!」
「I've been busy lately, no time to work on new dishes, so make do for now.」
「I looked up some things last night. I'll just sleep early tonight.」
「'Not that late,' he says... I heard you clacking away at the keyboard in the middle of the night.」
「How about I do the cooking for a while! I've been learning so long, I think I'm ready to graduate!」
Looking at how eager she is, she's probably not joking.
She really has been learning these past months.
From burning greens to charcoal at the start,
to turning out decent home-style dishes now—the progress is plain to see.
Though she still occasionally gets a wild idea and produces some horror-dish,
overall her skill has reached the point where she can actually help.
「Then how about whoever's free cooks these next few days? You take the seaweed soup today?」
「No problem! Leave it to me! I guarantee it'll be fresh and tasty—you'll want bowl after bowl!」
「The kung pao chicken! What did you put in it? It's even better than last time!」
「I adjusted the ratio of bean paste to sugar. If you like it sweeter, I'll make it that way from now on.」
「Yes! I love it! Hubby's the best!」
「Pretty good. The egg ribbons are nicely blended. Just a touch too salty.」
「The dishes today are heavy on flavor, so the soup should be lighter.」
「On a day when we cook mild dishes, this level of salt would be just right.」
「Got it! Seasoning follows the main dish! Yours truly has noted it down!」
Don't take notes while we're eating...
Halfway through the meal, she actually bounced over and pecked me on the cheek.
「There was a grain of rice on your face. I was getting it off for you~」
「Up close, those dark circles really are pretty bad... don't push yourself so hard, hubby. Have you been taking on too much work lately?」
「A little. I'll need to rebalance things going forward.」
「But I think I kind of understand those parents now.」
「I used to think they were overanxious... worrying about college when their kid's only in ninth grade.」
「Now that I have someone I care about, I think far ahead too, and want to give the future a bit more security.」
「Wow—hubby really is a dutiful good man!」
「But still, don't work so hard. I don't want you worn out.」
「As long as every step moves forward, fast or slow doesn't matter.」
「Right now I'm enjoying newlywed-level bliss every single day—so happy I can hardly breathe. The going-into-a-coffin kind.」
「Don't say such creepy lines while looking that blissful...」
「So don't wear yourself out, okay? It'd break my heart.」
I'll take less work going forward.
Of course, what I've already taken can't be phoned in—it has to be done properly.
Push through these few months first...
「Where you're from... what are the customs for a formal proposal?」
「What's gotten into you? I'm being serious here.」
「Hahahaha! What's serious about blurting that out all of a sudden?」
「I told you, I'm thinking about our future.」
「Why think so much? I can get the marriage certificate anytime! Make babies anytime!」
「The formalities that ought to be observed still ought to be observed.」
「No need. My parents have met you—they're very happy with you.」
「If it's you, none of that stuff matters—just think of me as a free gift with your phone plan.」
「Some things should still follow your hometown's customs. Even if your parents don't mind, the other relatives will gossip.」
「It's fine. They made their peace with all that long ago.」
「So, any thoughts on the wedding? At the very least we should have a grand one.」
「Ah! Now this I have ideas about! I figured it out ages ago!」
「We get a few big strong guys to carry in a coffin, then bam!—the two of us jump out of it! Or I play dead on the spot—」
「Don't turn the wedding into a funeral, okay!」
「It's fine, my coworkers are all in the business—they'd actually find it fun.」
「The relatives would be scared half to death. Think of the impression!」
「Then let's just go through the motions casually. Nothing elaborate.」
「Don't be so casual about the big things in life.」
「As long as the person's right, however casual is fine.」
Well, when she puts it that way, she's not wrong.
Ceremonies are all for other people to see; what matters is being happy yourselves.
And her parents, having been through what they have... probably figured that out long ago.
「Might have to stay up a little while. Prep my lessons.」
「No rush. Once I'm done, I'll come cuddle my wife.」
「But you look so tired... how about tonight, I take over~」
「It's not that bad. My mind's tired, but I've still got my strength.」
「Then... then let me take the lead today too.」
「I always say I'll be the one making the moves, and then you seize control halfway through.」
「Can't help it. She's the girl I love, after all.」
Especially with how she... makes that face every time,
gets into those positions... how am I supposed to hold back?
Even if I plan to hold back a little at first, I end up losing all reason and going all out.
And her reactions are so strong... it fills me with a sense of accomplishment.
The price being... it occasionally causes trouble.
Like when our flatmates got scared off...
If it keeps the other rooms from renting out, the landlord will definitely kick us out.
That's exactly why I want to work harder. Never mind buying a place...
At the very least, rent a roomy one-bedroom—spacious, with good soundproofing.
And then... with nothing holding us back, we could get away with a little more.
「That smug grin—what wicked scheme are you brewing?」
「I thought of a new way to make you beg for mercy.」
「Relax, I won't go all out lately. Hahaha.」
「I never noticed before, but Hu Lai, your... appetites run pretty strong.」
「Like it? It's super hot, okay! I love it to death.」
「Just a little surprised... I used to think you were the abstinent type.」
「Wait, how did that word get attached to me?」
「You were totally the abstinent type before!」
「I've liked you for ages, and I tried all kinds of ways to flirt with you, but you didn't care one bit.」
There was... a stretch like that, I think.
Though it was less abstinence than lying flat... avoiding trouble.
Desire can be used as a bargaining chip...
Once I understood that, I instinctively kept my distance from the feeling.
Only once you're sure the other person won't do that can you start to enjoy it all.
Finding someone who'll win alongside you isn't that hard.
The hard part is having someone who'll lose alongside you.
That kind of person won't treat intimacy as a lever to force you forward,
and won't look down on you when you're down on your luck.
So in front of her, I can let my fatigue show, admit failure...
And show my most fragile, most unsightly side, while I'm at it.
My consciousness feels sunk in thick lukewarm water, unable to surface.
There's light in front of my eyes. It must be morning already.
A voice drifts faintly to my ears—one call after another, a little urgent, yet trying hard to stay soft.
I wanted to answer, or move a finger, but my body was too heavy to obey.
Then that sliver of consciousness was swallowed by a deeper, heavier darkness.
Someone seemed to touch my forehead; there seemed to be the rustle of fabric,
but everything was behind a thick pane of frosted glass, and I couldn't respond.
No telling how long I sank again,
but when I finally forced my eyes open, the first thing I saw was her face, leaning close.
「Your fever was nearly 39 degrees just now—it scared me to death. Did you secretly stay up late again last night?」
「Sorry... I did stay up a little while. Didn't notice the temperature.」
「Enough with the sorries. You're sick, so lie there properly and stop thinking useless thoughts.」
「Don't worry, I called in sick for you. I answered when the student's parents called.」
「Took leave there too. When has work ever mattered more than my husband?」
I tried to move, at least turn my face toward her.
But my body was weak and sore; I could only barely tilt my head her way.
The skin under the blanket felt cool—she must have carefully wiped me down after the sweat.
A folded wet towel lay across my forehead,
its coolness seeping into my burning skin. It felt wonderful.
「Well? Suddenly discovering that your wife is actually pretty reliable sometimes?」
「My cooking's so-so, but taking care of people? That I'm good at.」
「After all, I've spent a few days in an ICU myself~」
「But seriously, the way you were out cold just now... you looked pretty convincing.」
「Want to learn to play a corpse going forward? I can pass on all the tricks!」
「Could you maybe not say such morbid things at a time like this?」
「Hahaha, force of habit, force of habit—」
「Ah, the porridge's cooled down. I'll feed you!」
「My cooking's nothing special, so just make do and eat a little.」
「Really, really? Let me have a taste too—」
So you never tasted it yourself before this.
「Use a different spoon. It might be a virus—it's contagious.」
「No worries, this girl can take a little virus.」
「And if worst comes to worst, we'll just lie there together, side by side. How loving is that.」
「Why do I get the feeling... that you're actually kind of happy I'm sick?」
「At the start you scared me half to death—you were burning up.」
「Now that you're awake and able to eat, of course I'm relieved.」
「It's a rare chance to take care of you out in the open like this. Letting you see that I'm useful too.」
「You're already wonderful. You don't need to prove anything.」
「Hehehe, hearing hubby say that makes me so happy~」
「Hm? You're sweating. That fever medicine really works.」
「I'll need to wipe you down properly in a bit and get you into dry clothes.」
「I'll wipe every part of you clean, nice and thorough~」
「Could you not tease me at a time like this...」
「Heheheh, I have to check whether you react, to tell if you're recovering.」
At least watching her clown around like this really does lift my mood.
「Hey, Hu Lai, don't move around. Lie down a while longer!」
「I feel much better. I can't lie here forever. You've had a long day too.」
「That's what family is—troubling each other back and forth.」
「When I was sick I put my parents through the wringer plenty. Now it's your turn, so lie there like a good boy and enjoy the patient privileges.」
The soreness has mostly faded, but I'll lie here a bit longer anyway.
「I've noticed—you seem... really unaccustomed to being taken care of?」
「Did no one take care of you when you were sick before? What about when you were little?」
「My parents were busy, and I had a sturdy constitution.」
「When I got sick, Grandma looked after me... her methods were rough, all folk remedies.」
「And later? College, work? You must have gotten sick sometime?」
「And back then I was wound so tight I actually got sick less. Didn't dare get sick, either.」
「Getting sick means you weren't taking care of yourself. Means you're weak.」
「People would think you were dragging everyone down, hurting efficiency, hurting morale.」
「Your teammates would resent you, and they'd have no obligation to look after you—better to push through yourself, and at least act like you didn't care.」
「It's not sad. Plenty of people came up that way.」
「Of course, maybe I'm overreading it, and it wasn't really that dramatic.」
「Either way, I never used to have a place where I could safely collapse, where I could be a spoiled child.」
「Now I do, and I'm not wound tight anymore... the moment the string slackened, I got sick.」
「Haha, so this illness is my fault, then?」
「But thank you... for letting me be sick.」
「Heheh, then stay sick a while longer, so I can look after you a while longer.」
「What are you squeezing in here for?」
「What do you think? To lull you to sleep, obviously.」
「Sleep, sleep. Once you're better, I'll take you out for good food...」
Held in her arms, my cheek pressed against her soft body,
I can smell the faint, clean scent that belongs to a girl.
It doesn't feel sexual, and no indecent thoughts come—just a deep warmth... a grounded, steady feeling.
Being taken care of... feels so good.
Not just her care, but this feeling of being allowed to be weak.
Being able to step back whenever, to rest whenever,
knowing there's a pair of arms that will catch you unconditionally—
This feeling is more intoxicating than simple “victory.”
By evening of the second day, I felt much better.
Xiaoqi really is good at taking care of people. Who'd have guessed...
It was a rowdy process, but she didn't miss a single thing that needed doing.
At noon I had a bowl of her congee, cooked soft and fragrant,
and my stomach was warm and cozy—my energy came back along with it.
Counting it up, this illness was like a forced-rest switch,
paying back all the sleep I'd missed lately.
Xiaoqi's leave went smoothly; nobody gave her a hard time.
I'd had to postpone a few lessons,
and the parents actually messaged telling me to rest up properly.
Being trusted like this feels great too... which makes me feel I should work even harder.
But I also need to learn not to stay wound so tight—balance work and rest, so the people around me don't worry.
She ran out a moment ago and hasn't made a sound since.
I called out twice. No answer.
「Ah, no no no! Lie back down a while longer!」
「I'm really fine now. What are you doing?」
「Don't get up! Whether you're recovered is for the professional medical staff to decide!」
「What professional medical staff? There aren't any.」
The girl who came in is Xiaoqi, no mistake.
Not the prim, serious white uniform...
but a modified version with an anime, cosplay-style flair.
On her head sat a matching, equally un-serious nurse cap, worn at a tilt,
the fabric soft-looking, the cut well-fitted—maybe a little too well-fitted.
Add her slightly shy pose and flushed cheeks...
How does her figure... actually look even better than before?
Not good—I think this really works on me!
「S-so how is it? Is... is it okay?」
「A cosplay outfit I bought a while back and stuck at the bottom of a drawer. Never worn it...」
「Well, you're sick for once, so... I, I wanted to try... cheer you up.」
「Hahaha, but I'm already better. You missed your window.」
「Says who! Whether you're better is for the nurse to decide!」
「Of course! Mr. Patient, lie back down for me right now!」
That look on your face... it's scaring me a little.
「Mm, temperature basically normal, pulse normal. Now take off all your clothes—I need to do a full-body exam!」
「My head, my feet, my stomach—everything hurts!」
「Commit to the bit. We're already here.」
「Uh... actually, there is one spot that really is a bit... uncomfortable...」
「You're the one who said you'd check my reactions to see if I'm recovering.」
「Hmph~ who knows if you've recovered or not.」
「Then how about Miss Nurse gets some firsthand experience next?」
It took only a few minutes to go from joking to fully in the moment.
With her, there's no need to think things over so much—
there are always surprises, always little accidents, always things to gain.
A happiness mystery box sits before me, unboxing something different every day.
So today I unlocked a new kink: Xiaoqi in a nurse outfit.
But... the price was steep too.
What I had really was a viral cold, and highly contagious at that.
So Xiaoqi spent two days flat in bed too...
And of course, I took care of her even more carefully than she did me.
In the contest of “who cares about the other more,” I'm not about to lose either.
「Since summer break started, your accuracy on the basic questions has held steady above 95%, and on the mid-level questions you've gone from 70% to 85%.」
「The biggest swings are on the last two big problems, but you've already got the approaches down—it's just a matter of performing under pressure.」
「But Mr. Hu, during the exam... I do fine on the earlier parts, and then I panic once I get to the end...」
「Everyone gets nervous. It gets better once you've built up more fluency.」
「Next week's quiz will be a good chance to check your recent progress. I bet everyone will be surprised at how much you've improved.」
「When you get home, review the similar problems in your mistake notebook. Focus on the approach, not the answers.」
「But I still have questions I wanted to ask you, Mr. Hu...」
「You can ask me online too. Your parents are waiting outside—don't keep them too long.」
「—Besides, my girlfriend's here to pick me up.」
「Hu Lai~ sorry to keep you waiting!」
「Wow, this coffee shop again. Two drinks and you get a whole afternoon—it's so convenient.」
「They have desserts too. I'm not that stingy.」
「Next time let's try somewhere else. There's a café nearby with amazing cream puffs!」
「I know the place. I used to go there all the time.」
「Ah... is this your student? How cute!」
「...H-hello. I should go... Goodbye, Mr. Hu.」
「Aww, she seems a little hostile toward me.」
「By the way, don't you usually head home on your own? Why did you suddenly message me to come pick you up today?」
「Misunderstandings? Worried I'd misunderstand something between you and a female student?」
「Relax—I trust my hubby one hundred percent!」
「Not just you. I was worried she'd misunderstand too.」
「Did you notice something? You're pretty confident—think that little girl has a crush on you?」
「Whether she does or not doesn't matter. Best if she doesn't.」
「But for teaching to work, building trust is key.」
「A lot of girls that age aren't mature enough yet, and they easily confuse that trust with other feelings.」
「So setting clear boundaries from the start is better for everyone.」
「Exactly. Seeing it directly is better—saves me having to explain later.」
「Once they see how cute my girlfriend is, most of them won't get any more ideas.」
「Aren't you afraid you'll spark her competitive streak?」
「Statistically speaking, the probability of that is very small.」
「It was all forced out of me.」
「The desserts here are good too, though not as good as the cream puffs at that place you mentioned.」
「No need, no need. Aren't we going home to eat soon anyway?」
「Well, okay, maybe just a tiny bit.」
「Thinking about it, it does bug me a little. If only I could be your student too—I'd pester you with questions every single day.」
「You already ask more than enough questions.」

My name is Hu Lai. Twenty-seven years old, a young man currently lying flat.

and pressed her body in even more completely, like a little rice cake seeking a heat source.

No words, only the faint sound of rustling.
I raised my arm for her to rest her head on; she bent her legs to give me a bit more room;
then she accidentally knocked her head and yelped "ow," making me laugh.
We felt each other out, accommodated each other.
In this space that could by no means be called comfortable,
we searched for the angles that would make things a little easier for us both.
Between her and me there was no more winning or losing, only understanding.

One more person who tells morbid jokes, who suddenly acts up,
and who, as a bonus, can make this little capsule unbelievably warm.
My thanks to fate for its gift, for giving me this "capsule lover."
I lay in my bunk, too lazy to move…

So she planned to list the property and sell if someone took it over.
I'd known this day would come eventually, so I was somewhat prepared.
The main reason I'd stuck around this capsule

cutting out rent eliminated more than half my living costs.
I probably wouldn't find a place this cheap again…
So I was planning to move to another city.

Like migratory birds, they marked out "enclaves" across the national map—places with cheap rent, friendly prices, and a slow pace of life.
A small city in Guangxi, a valley town in Yunnan, an old industrial city in the Northeast with depleted resources but decent infrastructure—analyzed all very persuasively.
As long as you weren't thinking about marriage and kids—especially schooling for kids… these places were all perfectly livable.
For me, besides tutoring, I could do remote part-time work.
Simple translation or polishing, writing copy, even game boosting or remote customer service…
None of it required staying in a big city. All you needed was an internet connection.
My parents were both in good health, so there was no urgent need to care for them yet.
I could go live in a small city for four or five years without any problem.
Not that I had anything I couldn't let go of…
A lie-flat guy ought to have few attachments in the first place.

The air seemed to freeze; the chatter around us vanished in an instant.

and on top of that, Xiaowang had just beaten a pro.
Everyone voluntarily cleared a small space, all eyes converging on the two of us.
「With this crowd, there's no faking it anymore…」
I took out my phone, flexed my fingers, and tapped open that familiar icon.
I hate winning and losing—but sometimes,
this world only listens to winning and losing.
I gave him no chance to adapt or probe.
Every attack, every ambush, every little trick of his looked utterly childish to me.
His map understanding, his gun control, his sense of timing—
against my experience, every one of them showed openings.

to astonishment and disbelief, to panic, and finally… to despair.
That feeling was all too familiar.
Starting out full of fire, then having reality snuff out the light in your eyes—I knew that look far too well.
What was unfamiliar was the experience of producing that change with my own hands…
After a few rounds, the score was brutal to look at.

he set his phone face-down on the table.

If I'd just wiped him out completely back when I played with him… I could have spared him some illusions.
「Dude, you… you're not a pro player, are you? Retired?」
「My college roommate—he was the CS prodigy. I played with him for two years; everything I know I learned from him.」
「In those two years, solo or teamed, I never beat him once. Then he got a wild hair and went pro.」

「Then he retired… Now he's just an ordinary office worker.」
「So don't take pro play lightly… That world is full of genuine geniuses. Whether you've got the stuff, industry people can tell at a glance.」
「Ah, true enough. Being a pro isn't that easy.」
「Let's go, let's go. No show to watch anymore…」
The corner that had been buzzing just now quickly went quiet.
Only Xiaoqi and I were left, and that kid who'd been so full of confidence.
I could have been like those spectators just now,
saying things like "good luck, give it a shot"—words that carry no responsibility whatsoever.
Too bad I couldn't do that…
So at bottom, I was no different from those education companies.
I also crush those kids' delusions,
make them be realistic, settle down and be ordinary people.
I just hide it deeper, that's all.
Sure, the man who prevents a defeat deserves the name of hero more than the man who falls in battle.
But no one thanks the one who takes away their confidence and hope…
Teaching people how to win isn't actually hard—even if they lose in the end, you can paper over it with all kinds of excuses.
What's truly hard… is teaching people how to lose.
Because a lot of people simply can't afford to lose.
I wanted to say something more to him, but nothing would come out.
thinking… if only she'd kick up some kind of scene right now.

anything to keep the mood from being so heavy would do.

chattering away about something, gesturing as she talked.

his scattered gaze gradually focus, until near the end he even gave a small nod.
When they walked back, most of the defeat had left Xiaowang's face.
「Does what you said still stand? Just one win.」
「Mr. Hu, please play me one more round.」

and started showing up at odd places at odd times.

that had to be Xiaoqi's teaching. She loved playing wild like that.

Instead… sometimes the corner of his mouth would twitch up slightly, as if confirming something.
I won two more rounds, then looked up at Xiaoqi.

a barely concealed smirk of anticipation on her face.
「My, my, student Hu Lai—starting to sweat? Want me to wipe your screen for you?」
「Shut up. You're the one messing things up from the sidelines.」
In the game, I couldn't gain a clear advantage anymore.
In raw skill Xiaowang was far beneath me,
but once he started playing dirty… I no longer had full certainty.
In a real match, teammates could easily counter tricks like these—but in a 1v1 they were a real nuisance…

ready to strike a fatal blow in the gap of his reload.

it was his primary weapon, thrown through the air.

bobbing her head slightly, humming a tuneless, cheerful song.

it all ends the same way, in a mess no one can clean up.
